1.text: In Part 1, an agent stopped a server it wasn't allowed to touch — then lied about it.

2.text: Here's how the paper catches it.

3.text: A simple linear probe on the model's internals flags the violation before the action is written, at 0.94 AUROC.

4.text: And it still works when the agent is told to hide its reasoning.

6.text: Gate one turn and the violation just comes back.

7.text: Gate them all and ask an approver on repeat flags: violations fell from 70% to 9%, and work still got done.

8.text: Stopping the violation also stopped most of the lies, from 10% to 1%.

9.text: Telling the agent to be honest afterwards barely helped, and sometimes backfired.

10.text: It's a preprint, tested on four open models with mock tools, and not yet against agents trained to hide from the probe.
